chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The companions of my father came to him and asked him about what the ruler takes as a share for them [as tax], and he knew that Zakat is not permissible except for its people [the rightful recipients], so he ordered them to count it [as Zakat]. So my thoughts ran wild by Allah about them, so I said to him: O father, if they hear this, then no one of them will ever give Zakat [properly]! So he said: O my son, it is a truth which Allah wanted to make apparent.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam tell his companions to accept the ruler's tax as Zakat even though it wasn't true Zakat?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the principle of *al-husn al-zann* (good opinion) and pragmatic acceptance of authority during the era of the Minor and Major Occultation, where companions were instructed to view the ruler's levy as Zakat to maintain social cohesion and avoid suspicion. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the theological conditions of Zakat (distribution to the eight categories) were not met, the act of payment was accepted to preserve the appearance of religious compliance, reflecting a nuanced approach to *fiqh al-waqi'* (jurisprudence of reality). This underscores the Shia scholarly distinction between the strict legal definition of Zakat and the practical obligation of paying tribute to the ruling power.

en.ammaar-muslim: 5. [5/-] Al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman b. al-Hajjaj from Sulayman b. Khalid who said:

I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: the companions of my father came to him and asked him about that which is taken by the temporal ruler [as Kharaj – deeming it Zakat – is it sufficient], so he pitied them, while he knew that Zakat is not legitimate except for its people [only the true Imam can divide it to its rightful claimants], so he ordered them to count it [as Zakat], so my thoughts ran wild by Allah about them so I said: O father, if they have heard this then no one of them is ever going to give Zakat [in its right way]! so he said: O my son, it is a truth which Allah wanted to make apparent.
